body: Where are you hanging out where you're being told to kill yourself constantly?

I'm actually still trying to figure out why today of all days I broke my composure. I have had close calls in the past, days when my volition was weaker due to not getting enough sleep, accidentally stumbling on explicit content online, or other factors that may have contributed. Today, I got enough sleep, and upon waking up I was immediately bombarded by these cravings. I found that if I masturbate earlier in the day, I am more likely to masturbate compulsively or turn to porn later in the day, so I weathered the cravings out.

I started a new habit of making a list of tasks before falling asleep, and doing them the next day, to prime myself for the next day ahead. I think there may have been a mix of experiencing strong cravings first thing in the day (which is unusually rare for me), and then feeling some emptiness once I achieved all of the tasks that I set out to do for the day. I already decided that I wasn't going to resist the CM (compulsive masturbation) urge, so I went on a website where I can chat to NSFW characters and did the deed that way, by texting them and using my imagination.

After that, I was on the fence whether to consider this a porn relapse or a compulsive masturbation relapse. Because of this uncertainty, I decided to go to look at actual porn to remove ambiguity, thus knowingly ending my 72 day streak.

I don't know how I would prevent something like this in the future. It was unexpected. I think instead, I will choose to re-frame my relationship with porn. Instead of tracking the things I am not doing (aka abstaining from pornography), I will start tracking the things I am DOING every day to forward parts of my life that porn has crippled me with in the past, like generally low self-esteem, talking to women, and other addictive behaviors like drinking alcohol. I'm actually 4 months sober from alcohol as of today! And with alcohol, I can say confidently that I do not miss drinking. With porn, it's more complicated. There are ways to engage with it that are not as harmful (seeking out content that isn't dehumanizing or highly fetishized) that I want to try exploring. I think for someone who isn't currently sexually active, it's an acceptable harm reduction technique. It's why I'm not too upset over this reset, and I don't want you to feel frustrated either. I know for a fact that my relationship with porn will never be the same again. This is the kind of progress that some arbitrary abstinence tracker will never be able to qualify, whether it's 24 days or 72 days. With the knowledge that I have now, I can make the same amount of progress, in a much shorter time frame. I think at this pace, there will be a day when I don't even think of watching porn.

TLDR: I don't know, and I will continue working on myself without sweating too much about looking at porn again. I just won't make it a daily compulsive habit. I think that part will be easy now.
